El tejido es una de las expresiones más: Weaving is one of the most vibrant expressions of Aymara culture. In the Putre highlands, families still spin and weave alpaca and llama wool, animals that besides providing a livelihood are an essential part of the Andean worldview.
El awayo —la manta multicolor que se usa: The awayo —the multicolored cloth used for carrying, keeping warm and decorating— is perhaps the most recognizable textile: it is part of daily life as well as ceremonies and patron saint festivals.
\"Sawuña\": el oficio de tejer se transm: "Sawuña": the craft of weaving is passed down from generation to generation, mostly among women.
Hoy, artesanas y artesanos de Putre mant: Today, Putre's artisans keep the traditional loom alive and offer their weavings, ceramics and woodwork to visitors: a genuine chance to take a piece of this culture home with you.
El calendario aymara se mide en ciclos a: The Aymara calendar is measured in farming cycles, rituals and patron saint festivals that set the rhythm of the year in Putre. Many celebrations blend Andean tradition with the Catholicism that arrived centuries ago. If your visit falls on one of these dates, don't miss it.
